plans.position: Prospective breadth: make the live prospective record the measure of the goal, and widen what it covers now, during the Q3 2026 earnings season. That means a second and then a third theme, the held-out names as live coverage, and Scout plus signal scans every week. Keep replays as cheap, model-free smoke tests of the code scorer. Do not spend Researcher sessions or double-blind review on runs as of 2025.
plans.thesis: Both readers in the scorecard are contaminated, and its own text says so. The session model has read 2025 (ticket 29, protocol step 3). Leakage is worse than the as-of bound can catch, because the model's memory steers which documents it searches and which quotes it picks, even when every Fact is genuinely from the period. The "leak-free" code reader is partly fitted too: the cue "two players" is in signals.yaml because the AXT case study named it (docs/experiments.md, ticket 18 caveat). The cases are winners and losers chosen after the fact, with quotes "chosen knowing the outcome" (docs/research/early-signal-case-studies.md, Limits), and seven cases "are no hit rate" (ticket 29, step 5). The only test that neither the model's memory nor the case selection can touch is a call dated before the outcome exists. Atlas already has that instrument (ticket 19: call_record, settle_calls, predictions). But the record is not yet scoreable. There are 22 calls, 17 name AXT, and all were made 12 to 18 October, so they amount to roughly one bet. 8 of 22 carry no direction. There are no silence rows. So the honest next step is to make the record scoreable and broad, not to run more replays.

plans.how_progress_on_the_goal_is_measured: By the prospective record, pre-registered in the map before results arrive. Weekly process numbers: calls per week by theme and origin; the share of calls with a direction (now 14 of 22); silence rows per week; distinct company-chokepoint clusters among calls (now about 1); themes covered (now 1); trust gate on scheduled sessions at or below 10% (ticket 17's bar); proposal-to-judgement latency. Outcome numbers at each checkpoint: fundamental settlement first, meaning the share of Belief calls whose next-report expectation is met when the next report lands (first in January and February 2027); then each directed call's +3 and +6 month change against its theme's equal-weighted benchmark; and the false-positive rate on silence and control names (eToro, Snap, POET). The decision threshold is fixed now. For a one-sided test of a 70% against a 50% base rate at 80% power, about 37 independent calls are needed (my calculation), so the record is judged when it holds at least 30 independent clusters across at least 3 themes, expected around April to June 2027. Before that, every number is reported as a count, never as a rate. Replay ranks are reported as smoke tests of the scorer, not as progress on the goal.

risks: Slow verdict: the prospective record cannot score the method before roughly Q2 2027, and it cannot steer development week to week. The cheap code-reader replays and the per-theme precision reads have to carry steering until then.

Selection bias moves rather than disappears: the lead and the owner choose themes and seeds knowing 2025 to 2026 winners. Mitigations: a seed rule written before choosing, silence rows over the whole scanned universe, an equal-weighted theme benchmark. They reduce the bias, they do not remove it.

Calls are correlated within a theme and within a season (all four case names made their lows on 7 to 9 April 2025, a market-wide sell-off). Effective N is far below the call count, which is why the threshold counts independent clusters.

Human review is the throughput ceiling: Belief calls are dated at the proven judgement, which waits on the lead and owner (15 split Beliefs pending) and on the luna window. Breadth may queue Beliefs faster than they can be judged. Signal calls avoid this but carry 40% noise (12 of 20 precision).

The agent path is barely proven: the first scheduled Skeptic opened no session (map, 16 Oct), and no scheduled Scout has yet produced a signal call. If the CronJobs are unreliable, breadth yields nothing.

Memory-packaging is half-blind without Samsung, Kioxia and the Korean and Japanese filings (20a out of scope). An absent call there may reflect missing sources, not silence, so silence rows must name the documents read.

The scorer may not generalise: it caught 4 of 14 key sentences in the case study, and it has no predicate for market-level statements or supply discipline. A broad record could be quiet because of the scorer, not the world, and only the Scout's own reading guards against that.
The Claude weekly budget and the ChatGPT 5 h window: two or three themes of agents plus judging may exhaust them mid-week. The CronJobs need a per-week cap and the lead must watch it.
plans.against_the_current_plan: Publishing the Hypothesis (done) and landing 20a and 21 are right, and this plan keeps them first. The fault is that the order then spends the scarcest budgets, Researcher sessions and blind review by the lead and owner, on 29a and the as-of-2025 session runs. That measurement admits leakage it cannot bound: the model's memory steers what it searches even when every Fact is as-of bounded. Its "leak-free" code reader carries the AXT-derived cue "two players". It runs on seven cases chosen after the fact, which by its own text are "no hit rate". Meanwhile the live record, the one uncontaminated instrument, has fixable gaps that leave it nearly unscoreable. 17 of its 22 calls name AXT, all made in one week: effectively one bet. 8 have no direction because signal_call and hypothesis_call write direction=None. It has no silence rows, so it cannot show staying quiet. No signal-origin call has been made yet. The plan also leaves breadth after the scorecard. That wastes the Q3 2026 earnings season, which starts now: calls dated on this season's transcripts are the first that can settle on fundamentals in January and February 2027. Reorder: 20a and 21 land, the record fix ticket, agents on two themes, 29's companies as live controls, a third theme by a written seed rule, and code-reader replays only as smoke tests.

plans.position: Owner-decision loop: make the product of Atlas a weekly ranked bottleneck watchlist across themes. Each item is a thesis with a checkable confirmation trigger and a checkable falsifier. A notice goes out when either fires, and the owner's act/watch/pass is recorded beside the outcomes of every item, passed and unlisted ones included. Ticket 29's leak-free code reading should still run. Its roughly ten Opus session runs should wait.
plans.thesis: The objective ends in one act, the owner's bet. The case studies say the value lies in having a thesis ready and being told when it confirms, not in being first: entry on the explicit confirmation was still AXT 14.5x and SanDisk 8.4x at six months (docs/research/early-signal-case-studies.md, point 3; memory note early-bottlenecks-beyond-ai-capex). Atlas already has every part: archive signals, the Scout, Beliefs, a published Hypothesis, a predictions table that settles from a Fact, an XBRL observation or a price, belief_confirmed notices, and the call record. Nothing turns them into a weekly decision. The forward measure as built does not measure the goal: production holds 22 calls, 17 naming AXT, 8 with no direction, on a stock already about 60x from its 2025 low, and 0 predictions. Ticket 29's scorecard is neither leak-free nor selection-free (seven cases the owner named after the outcome, and the session model read 2025 in training). A forward loop that records every listed item, every pass and the unlisted signal hits is the one measure that is both by construction. Its cost is that it yields engagement data now and accuracy only in months.

plans.against_the_current_plan: The order publish -> 20a/21 -> 29a -> scorecard runs measures the goal in two ways, and neither fits it. (1) The prospective record as built measures late, correlated statements. GET /api/v1/calls returns 22 calls, all photonics: 21 from Beliefs, 1 from the Hypothesis, 17 naming AXT, 8 with no direction. All were made in October 2026 on a stock about 60x its 2025 low (AXT $1.35 on 2025-05-01, $85.87 on 2026-10-02, per the case studies). The 2026-11-18 checkpoints will measure AXT's momentum against its peers, one thesis counted seventeen times, not Atlas's earliness. GET /api/v1/predictions returns 0. The Hypothesis's measurable_predictions and falsifiers are prose with no range or deadline, so nothing will tell the owner when the thesis confirms or breaks. Case-study items 3 (a tracked management forecast) and 4 (a notice on confirmation; proposed updates fire only on contradiction) are still open. (2) The scorecard's session runs are the most expensive part (about 10 Opus sessions plus two blind reviewers each) and the least trustworthy: the model read 2025 in training, and leakage helps the negatives as much as the positives, since the model also knows eToro and Snap fell. Seven owner-named cases are 'no hit rate', as ticket 29 says itself. Its leak-free half, the code reading, is cheap and should run. Neither half changes what the owner can decide next week. The plan also has no step where the owner's decision is the output, and no surface where a cue becomes a thesis with a trigger. 20a and 21 are right and stay: they supply a second theme and the page the watchlist links into.

plans.position: Scorecard-first. Run ticket 29 next, before building anything new. Before the first session, add three leakage controls to its protocol (dated, below the fixed key) and a miss taxonomy chosen in advance. Then let the classified misses decide the next build. Begin a cohort dated after the model's training cutoff now, as the held-out set that keeps renewing.
plans.thesis: Atlas's process measures are close to their ceiling: Fact precision is 92-100% and the trust gate 4%. They no longer say whether Atlas calls a bottleneck early (.scratch/pilot/results.md, "The MCP session"). The prospective record cannot answer that soon either. Of its 22 calls, 17 name AXT, a bottleneck priced in October 2025; the benchmark includes AXT; the first checkpoints fall on 12-18 November and the six-month ones in April 2027. That is one correlated, late bet, so the effective sample is about 1 (GET /api/v1/calls, 2026-10-18). Every candidate build so far (a market-level supply predicate, supply discipline, tracking a company's forecast) is justified only by sentences from two winners chosen after the fact (docs/research/early-signal-case-studies.md, "What it asks of Atlas"). Building any of them now is the bias the owner warned about. The scorecard costs about $120 of Claude subscription and two weeks. With a miss taxonomy fixed in advance and three leakage controls, it turns six held-out cases into a diagnosis of where the method fails, which is worth more than their hit count.

plans.how_progress_on_the_goal_is_measured: There are three numbers, reported side by side and never pooled. (2) The post-cutoff cohort, repeated monthly: of the constraints Atlas stated as of a date after the model's training cutoff, how many the next quarter's primary documents confirmed or contradicted, and on how many of the rule-chosen companies a session added something the code ranking did not. This is the only leak-free measure of earliness. (3) The prospective record (ticket 19), reported for what it can show: drift after confirmation on a thesis already priced, with about one independent bet. It does not show earliness until calls on bottlenecks not yet priced are in it. Process measures (precision, trust gate) are reported as guardrails only: a run counts only if they hold.

risks: Six scored cases is noise as a hit rate. A single outcome (for example the session missing SanDisk at 2025-02-28 because a transcript is missing) could swing the reading. The answer is the decision rule (two positive runs missing in the same class), but even that rests on very few cases.

Leakage cannot be removed from 2025 cases, only measured. The closed-book arm may show the model states every key from memory, leaving no 2025 case that discriminates. The scorecard would then report mainly code ranks and miss classes, and the post-cutoff cohort has to carry the weight.

Once the misses choose a build, the six cases are in-sample for evaluating that build. Measuring again on them would flatter the build, so the next measure has to come from a new post-cutoff as-of date.

Freeze it, score it pooled across the universe at every month on held-out cases and on controls chosen by a rule, record what it ranks as dated calls, and spend Opus sessions only on what it ranks. plans.thesis: The code track has already closed most of the gap the brief describes. The case study's "4 of 14" measured the Claim rule (`atlas.claims.directional_cue`), not the signals scorer. Run locally on paraphrases of the 14 key sentences in docs/research/early-signal-case-studies.md, with no transcript speaker factor, signals-v3 scores 9 of 14 above min_score. It scores 0 on the three negative-style sentences (Snap, eToro, "sufficient capacity"). Two of the five misses are only threshold effects: "The market is tight." is 20 characters against min_sentence_chars 25, and a bare "shortages" scores 0.4×2.0 = 0.8 against 1.5. The real gaps are three: supply discipline (underutilisation, "support pricing"), power/grid bottlenecks (every IREN sentence scores 0), and paraphrase ("tsunami"). The code is the only reader that cannot know outcomes from data, costs no model call, and is cheap enough to run on controls and at every date. The owner's winners-bias warning needs exactly that. The concession comes first: the vocabulary was written from the AXT and SanDisk case studies (ticket 18, the header of configs/discovery/signals.yaml), so those two are in-sample for the scorer. The code is free of data leakage, not of fit. The five other names, IREN, eToro, Snap, POET and Raspberry Pi, are held out for it.

A lexical ceiling: 'tsunami', 'cannot keep up' variants and market-level statements in new wording will be missed. A regex scorer catches the way managements usually say scarcity, not every way, so recall on unseen themes may be low.

Base rates in a boom: in AI-capex 2025-26 bottleneck language may be everywhere, so a pooled rank may flag much of the universe. Precision is 12 of 20 in photonics, met narrowly, with misses from Item 1 and Item 7 risk wording.

The signal lives in call Q&A, investor days and conferences (case study point 4; the AXT replay's top 20 is mostly transcripts). Those come through TradingView under the owner's display-only override, with a per-minute cap, so scaling the engine scales that dependence and its terms exposure.

Code finds sentences, not theses. It cannot tell a holder from a squeezed buyer (Raspberry Pi), judge financing (IREN between August and November), or say who holds the chokepoint. A code call is a lead, never a Belief, and the owner bets on argued theses, so sessions stay necessary.

Price checkpoints score market moves, not whether a bottleneck was real; code-origin calls risk turning the record into a backtest. Keep them labelled leads and read them as detection, never as Evidence or a portfolio.
Speaker labels are wrong in some TradingView transcripts (pilot-fix 32), which corrupts the management and analyst factors.
plans.against_the_current_plan: The order is publish → 20a/21 → 29a → scorecard runs. (1) Ticket 21, a page, comes before any measure of the goal. (2) Ticket 29 runs the leaky reader, an Opus session whose model has read 2025, at every as-of date, before the free monthly code grid that would show which session runs are informative. (3) Ticket 29 scores the code's reading by rank within the company's own top 20, which says nothing for a negative and nothing about standing out from the universe. (4) It calls the code reading leak-free without declaring that AXT and SanDisk are in-sample for its vocabulary. (5) It has no controls chosen by rule, so it cannot answer the winners-bias warning. (6) The prospective record it reports beside: 20 of 22 calls name AXT or Lumentum, all dated a year after AXT priced, and no call originates in the code. It measures persistence, not earliness.

critiques.best_graft: Each Belief-origin call states what the company's next report should show (backlog, lead time, allocation, price, a management forecast), and a Fact from that report settles it under ticket 19's prediction rules. This is the only outcome measure that is uncontaminated, about 3 months out rather than 6 to 9, not a price backtest, and it matches item 3 of the case study ("a management forecast as a tracked falsifier", docs/research/early-signal-case-studies.md). A cheap add-on: freeze signals-v3 and judge the top 20 memory-packaging leads strictly before any vocabulary change, as an out-of-sample precision read.

A call there in October 2026 cannot show earliness, and an equal-weighted benchmark inside a theme that has already run does not fix that. The plan's mitigation (a seed rule written before choosing seeds) does not touch the choice of theme.

Step 7's seed rule is circular, and its pool is the wrong one. 'Suppliers and customers named in the seed companies' 10-Ks' needs seeds first. The 104 Candidates are photonics leads (all in state 'lead' on production), not a power-theme pool.

Its statistics do not hold together. The power calculation (37 calls, 70% against 50%, 80% power) is arithmetically right, but the threshold it sets is 30 clusters, about 72% power. The 50% base rate (of beating an equal-weighted benchmark that includes the call's own company) is never justified.

It underrates the scorecard's mitigations. Leakage helps the model on the negatives too, so the negatives and the code reader paired with the session's reading are a real if imperfect check (ticket 29, protocol step 3). The plan's prospective sessions use the same model, whose training knows which themes are hot, so its prior steers what it searches in prospective work as well.

It budgets in dollars ($25 to $45 a week), but the binding limit is the Claude subscription's weekly cap and the 5 h luna window (which ran out on 16 Oct). The plan sets no per-week cap mechanism, only 'the lead must watch it'.

SanDisk's key statements were made at an Investor Day and at conferences, not in 10-Qs or 10-Ks (case-study point 4). Whether the TradingView catalog reaches back to February 2025 events for a newly seeded company is not checked, so step 6's replay may have nothing to rank.

It is honest about its own risks: correlated calls within a season, review throughput as the ceiling, memory-packaging half-blind without Samsung and Kioxia, the scorer's blind spot for market-level statements.

fatal_flaws: It never closes the biggest leak, which is prior_work. On production, GET /api/v1/research/prior-work?theme=photonics&as_of=2025-08-31&company_ids=<axt> returns 114 standing AXT Facts from documents public by that date, with 12 sessions hidden. Those Facts were recorded by sessions dated 2026 that knew how AXT turned out. The researcher prompt (agent/prompts/researcher.md line 14) and SKILL.md line 22 tell every session to call prior_work first and to cite existing Facts rather than search again. So the AXT calibration run is handed the answer with no search at all, and the plan's query-provenance audit, which only looks at search arguments, cannot see it. The same thing happens across the SanDisk runs: the 2025-05-31 run inherits the 2025-02-28 run's Facts and Beliefs, which breaks the independence the plan counts on. The protocol needs a mode where prior_work is off or isolated (a scorecard theme with prior_work forbidden, or a fresh theme per run), or the session arm measures Atlas's earlier hindsight-chosen work, not the method.

Its own definition of a 'leak-adjusted hit' leaves the session nothing to be credited for on 2025 cases. A hit counts only if it passes the provenance audit AND either the closed-book probe does not state it OR the code ranks it 20 or better. SanDisk's NAND undersupply, IREN's power shortage and AXT's InP are famous, so the closed-book arm will almost surely state all three. Every leak-adjusted hit then needs a code rank of 20 or better, so the session can be credited only where the code already found the cue. It can never show the M2 case it most needs to test: the session finding what the code ranked low. The likely report is an empty leak-adjusted column next to a raw column nobody can trust.

The decision rule cannot fire in a way that means anything. There are two scored positive cases (SanDisk and IREN; Raspberry Pi is a squeezed buyer and AXT is calibration only). The rule needs the same miss class in two different cases, so it is decided by n=2. The likeliest outcome is 'no class reached two', and the plan names no fallback. That is two weeks of the main lever (sessions) spent with the next build still undecided, while it freezes signals tuning and defers the second theme's Hypothesis.
weaknesses: The M4 build trigger points at the wrong layer. The '4 of 14' finding (early-signal-case-studies.md, 'What Atlas would have done') tested the pipeline Claim predicate's directional_cue, not signals-v3 and not the session method. Session Facts and Beliefs have steps and statuses but no predicate. Meanwhile signals.yaml already holds under[\s-]?suppl (line 173), 'get enough' (line 170) and 'too fast' (line 167). A 'market-level supply predicate' build would repair the bulk pipeline, which the scorecard does not run.

The query-provenance audit would flag Atlas's own method as leakage. SKILL.md line 43 tells every session to search 'allocation', 'lead time', 'sold out', 'qualified', 'second source', 'export permit', and line 33 lists allocation and lead times as the demand_vs_supply step's evidence. Calling 'allocation' a key term that no prior read justified penalises the skill, not leakage. The skill itself was written from photonics and AXT ('export permit', 'second source'), so it is in-sample too, and the plan freezes it without saying so.

The closed-book probe is self-defeating as written. Asking the model with no tools 'under a prompt that forbids outside knowledge' measures whether it complies, not what it knows. A knowledge probe has to invite recall ('what do you know of X's supply position in H2 2025?'), or a 'not stated' verdict means nothing.

The judge load is underestimated. The plan assumes 25-40 luna calls per session, but since ticket 23 every record_fact is judged (the MCP session recorded 38 Facts), on top of judge_statement calls (about a fifth of 120 calls) plus each propose_belief and the thesis at close. That is closer to 60-80 per session, so 10 sessions are about twice the ChatGPT windows planned.

The timeline ignores the deploy path. 'Minutes of the lead's time' to start intake when 20a lands needs a release and a home-ops PR that the owner merges. The scorecard-theme companies (IREN, eToro, Snap, POET) cannot be ingested until 29a's universe config is released and deployed, so code readings for them on 21-22 October also need 29a built, integrated, released, deployed and its TradingView transcripts fetched within about three days.

Scorecard runs write into production state. Their Beliefs, Issues and Facts become standing records, and a scorecard Belief judged proven would create a call_record dated 2026 (ticket 19), polluting the prospective record. The plan does not say the scorecard Beliefs stay unjudged and outside the Skeptic, Scout and next_issue frontier.

29c is not an earliness measure. It settles 'did the next 10-Q confirm the stated constraint' over companies picked because their themes are known bottleneck themes. A shortage that is still running (InP, NAND) has a high base rate of being confirmed. That measures persistence, has no priced date and no lead time, and the model knows these companies' stories up to its cutoff. Calling it 'the only leak-free measure of earliness' oversells it.

The IREN pre-registration rests on a misreading. 'IREN's code rank will be weak because there are no power or grid terms' ignores the generic \bshortages?\b and supply-shortage patterns (signals.yaml lines 182-184), which match 'the escalating power shortage'. A wrong prediction would then teach the wrong lesson ('photonics-shaped vocabulary').

It opportunity-costs the objective. Calls made forward in time are the only ones free of leakage by construction, and the memory/packaging theme goes live with 20a. Deferring that theme's Hypothesis and Scout/Researcher runs for a two-week n=2 diagnostic delays the only source of calls on bottlenecks not yet priced, which is the gap the plan itself names in the prospective record.
what_it_gets_right: It shows the prospective record is about one correlated bet. Production GET /api/v1/calls gives 22 calls: 21 from Beliefs and 1 from the Hypothesis, 17 naming AXT, 17 made on 2026-10-18. The benchmark includes the call's own company (AGENTS.md, ticket 19). It measures drift after confirmation, not earliness.

It corrects ticket 29's claim that the code's reading 'cannot leak'. signals.yaml lines 7-9 say the vocabulary comes from the case studies, and docs/experiments.md (2026-10-15) admits 'two players' is there because of AXT. The SanDisk and AXT code ranks are in-sample.
It corrects what the negatives measure. The model knows eToro and Snap fell, so a false positive on them measures discipline, not leakage.
It freezes the configuration: signals-v3 at f0fe9ee (verified to be the last signals.yaml commit), and the exact model ID instead of agent/run.sh's default alias 'opus' (line 73).

It classifies misses from the tool trace into classes fixed in advance (not in archive / not surfaced / read but not recorded / recorded but not believed / misstated). That gives a diagnosis, not a hit count. session_tool_call.arguments is jsonb (migration 0109), while GET /sessions returns only a count (sessions/service.py line 92), so the read route it asks for is a real gap.
It starts SanDisk's TradingView intake early. Case study point 4 says three of SanDisk's six key documents were not earnings calls, and the Investor Day sits on the first as-of date.
It takes code readings before any session, so reviewers cannot be anchored by session output.
unsupported_claims: 'IREN's code rank will be weak, because the vocabulary has no power or grid terms': the generic shortage patterns (signals.yaml lines 182-184) match 'the escalating power shortage', so the premise does not support the prediction.

'Every candidate build so far (a market-level supply predicate...) is justified only by sentences from two winners': the 4-of-14 cue test was of the pipeline Claim predicate (atlas.claims.directional_cue), which the session method does not use; signals-v3 already absorbed 'undersupplied', 'can't get enough' and 'too fast'.

The query-provenance audit 'catches the leak... the model knowing where to look': it cannot see Facts reached through prior_work (114 standing AXT Facts as of 2025-08-31 on production), and it flags vocabulary the skill itself prescribes (SKILL.md line 43).
critiques.best_graft: Fix a miss taxonomy before any run and classify each miss from the session's recorded tool trace (M1 not in archive, M2 never surfaced, M3 read but not recorded, M4 recorded but not believed, M5 misstated, FP), together with a frozen configuration (scorer commit, skill and prompt versions, exact model ID). Add a scorecard mode with prior_work and the reuse of standing Facts switched off, so each run starts from the archive alone.

fatal_flaws: Its own watchlist is not selection-free either. Watchlist v0 (Ciena, AAOI, MACOM, Coherent, plus the AXT/Lumentum thesis) comes entirely from the 12-company AI-optics universe in configs/themes/ai-infrastructure.yaml, which was chosen in the middle of the boom. The plan rejects the call record because it measures 'AXT's momentum against its peers, one thesis counted seventeen times', and that objection hits its own forward loop just as hard. Every item and every 'unlisted' control is the same photonics factor, already priced by October 2026. It swaps one measure of photonics momentum for another and defers the only test that has negatives (eToro, Snap, POET) and dates before pricing.

The 'passes and unlisted signal hits as controls' machinery does not exist, and it would not be a control if built. A signal-origin call is made only when a Scout session opens a question Issue with a lead_id (AGENTS.md, ticket 19; .scratch/atlas-beliefs/issues/19-the-prospective-record.md). One AXT replay alone had 268 to 293 hits (docs/experiments.md, the 27b and 27 entries). Calling every hit gives hundreds of correlated rows from one sector against about 5 treated items. 'Counts, not rates' does not rescue a control set that is ten times the treatment and all one sector.

It moves decision-readiness, not earliness, which is the objective. In two weeks it yields a list of already-run names and the owner's act/watch/pass on about 5 items. In months it yields the relative moves of a correlated basket, by the owner's decision class. That measures one user's taste and the theme's beta, not whether Atlas names a bottleneck before the market prices it.
weaknesses: The budget arithmetic is inverted. It defers about $120 of session runs (about 10 × $12; the MCP session took 24.5 min and $11.87, .scratch/pilot/results.md, 'The MCP session') and adds $40 to $45 a week of agent spend, a Sonnet build ticket of 2 to 3 days, a release, a home-ops PR, and a new per-document luna judge loop on the ChatGPT 5 h window that Fact and Belief judging already contend for (the merchant Belief waited on that window: map.md, 2026-10-16). Within a month the watchlist costs more than it saves.

It overrides an agreement the owner made today. The map's 2026-10-18 entry records the owner agreeing that ticket 29 plus the prospective record is the goal's measure, in the order publish, 20a/21, 29a, the runs. Deferring the agreed runs is the owner's call to make. The plan presents it as a step.

Step 1 is narrower than it claims. A fact-sourced prediction settles only from the Fact's value_json quantity.value (backend/atlas/hypotheses/predictions.py, _fact_value: 422 fact_has_no_quantity). The plan's own examples, 'a US InP permit by a date' and 'Lumentum's substrate statement', are boolean or prose and cannot settle. Four of the five published falsifiers are qualitative. Only numeric measures such as AXT's InP backlog or revenue fit without a build.

No 'proposed met' detection exists. Settlement is a manual POST naming a fact_id, observation_id or day, and a fact-sourced trigger needs a session to record the Fact first. The notice is therefore gated on someone reading each new document. 'Mostly assembly' understates a new judge pipeline, and a noisy one: about 4 flags flip between identical runs.

It contradicts itself on confirmation notices. The thesis says belief_confirmed notices exist (ticket 26, AGENTS.md 'Research that compounds'), while 'against_the_current_plan' says case-study item 4 (a notice on confirmation) is 'still open'. Item 4 is partly met for Beliefs. Its real gap is that the notice needs a session's Fact.
'Nothing turns them into a weekly decision' ignores ticket 21, now in CI (the Hypothesis page as the product, with the theme's changes feed), and the Calls panel that already sits on the theme page.

The leakage critique of ticket 29 skips the mitigations the ticket already has: a statement no cited Fact carries is not scored, negatives measure what the model 'finds' without reading it, and the leak-free code reading is reported beside every session score with unsupported hits marked. The forward loop's Researcher is the same model, leak-free by construction, but it buys that by measuring nothing about earliness for months.

Recording the owner's 'act' and comparing returns by decision class edges toward return measurement of his bets, which map.md lists as out of scope ('portfolio sizing; price data; return measurement') and memory note atlas-is-research-not-backtesting warns against. The plan names the drift risk but builds rows for it anyway.

The second theme does not cure earliness. Memory/packaging seeds include SanDisk at about $1,720 from $36 (case studies), equally post-hoc. Nothing in the plan widens discovery to unseeded companies (Candidates, EDGAR FTS), which is where an early call outside the boom names would come from.
Minor inaccuracy: the first +1-month checkpoints are due 2026-11-12 (2 calls), 2026-11-15 (3) and 2026-11-18 (17), per GET /api/v1/calls next_due. The plan says 'the first due 2026-11-18'.
what_it_gets_right: Its production facts check out: GET /api/v1/predictions total 0; 22 calls (21 from Beliefs, 1 from the Hypothesis), 17 naming AXT, 8 with direction null, and the Hypothesis's own call is undirected; c872c68e v2's measurable_predictions and falsifiers are prose with no range or deadline; ticket 19's production box is unticked.
Counting atomic Beliefs as independent calls multiplies one AXT thesis by about 17. Reading the record by thesis is the honest unit.
It keeps ticket 29's leak-free code reading (scripts/signal_replay.py --as-of) with the answer key frozen in git, and names the negatives as the false-alarm test.

It ranks by evidence stage (cue, stated, first numbers, headline) and never by price, and it separates 'first numbers' from 'headline' confirmation using IREN (case studies, 'Five more names', point 2).
Its risk list is candid about survivorship in the confirmation-entry rule (two winners), the review load on the owner, and the judge's noise.
It keeps 20a and 21 and stops further photonics depth, consistent with the map.

These would be measures a Fact's quantity or an XBRL value can settle (AXT InP revenue or backlog in its next report, a Lumentum figure), plus one falsifier with a number. fatal_flaws: The held-out code score is decided before the run. Once AXT and SanDisk are declared in-sample, the frozen-v3 positives are IREN and Raspberry Pi. The plan itself says every IREN sentence scores 0 under v3: the case study's IREN quotes are 'the escalating power shortage' (bare `shortages?` at 0.4x2.0 = 0.8, under min_score 1.5) and 'That is the critical bottleneck' (no family has 'bottleneck'). So IREN is a known miss. Raspberry Pi is a squeezed buyer, and the plan concedes code cannot tell a squeezed buyer from a holder. eToro, Snap and POET are not in the archive at all: production /api/v1/companies lists 21 companies, none of them. The '0 on negatives' comes from three hand-written sentences. For a supply-cue lexicon, a fintech and an ad seller staying quiet is trivially true. Measure (1), the plan's headline number, therefore carries almost no information.

v4 is fitted to IREN, the held-out case, which breaks the plan's own rule ('vocabulary changes driven by a held-out case's sentences: forbidden'). Two of v4's changes, 'bottleneck/constraint nouns given a subject' and ''shortage' with a subject', are exactly the changes that turn IREN's two quoted sentences into hits. The 'blind' power family is to be written 'from the theme description'. The only written description is ticket 29's key ('Grid power for AI data centres is short; connections take years'), and that is the IREN answer. The lead who reviews it has read docs/research/early-signal-case-studies.md. A v4 gain on IREN shown 'beside' v3 will read to the owner as the scorer generalising when it is fit.

Code-origin weekly calls would turn the prospective record into a regex backtest. The owner agreed the record as half of the goal's measure (ticket 29, 'Why'), defined as 'what Atlas said, dated'. A pooled top-k of lexical hits, at the measured 12-of-20 precision, would add sentence-level 'calls' every week and drown the 22 Belief and Hypothesis calls. They would be settled against an equal-weighted benchmark of the same small universe, so in an AI-capex boom the result is mostly beta. The roadmap proposal (docs/research/proposed-roadmap-2026-10-04.md §6) says return measurement waits for licensed point-in-time data. Owner memory says Atlas is research, not backtesting. The plan names this risk and still proposes the change. It would also stay AXT-heavy: AXT and Lumentum hold most of the replay's top 8, and the per-company cap it relies on does not exist.

Routing sessions by the detector locks in the detector's blind spots. If the Researcher's seeds come from the highest pooled v3 signal, a theme the vocabulary lacks (power scores 0) never gets a session until someone writes its regex first. That runs against theme independence, which is a stated requirement (memory: later themes robotics, energy, quantum), and against the IREN-type physical bottleneck the scorecard is meant to test.
weaknesses: Pooled rank measures being the loudest in the universe, not whether a bottleneck is present. Once 20a's memory and packaging seeds land, a theme-wide NAND undersupply that Micron and peers also describe pushes SanDisk's pooled rank down: a correct detection scored as a miss. The objective is the bottleneck and who holds it, not one company standing out from an arbitrary, hand-built pool (the photonics universe was itself chosen around AXT).

The monthly grid has no pre-registered k and no recency window. The replay ranks every document public by the as-of date back to 2018: the AXT v3 top 20 includes Coherent 8-Ks from 2018-12-27 and 2023-08-16. Without a fixed lookback (--since) and k, 'the first month the key cue entered the pooled top-k' is cumulative and leaves room to pick parameters after seeing results.

False positives on controls are undefined. A control's hit can only be called false with an outcome label. Labelling it by price is the backtest the owner warned against. Labelling it by the lead's judgement brings in 2025 hindsight. The plan reports a 'base rate', which is not a false-positive rate. In 2025 many SIC 3674 firms had real shortages (HBM, CoWoS, substrates).

The control rule does not fit the one held-out physical case. SIC 4911-type 'electric services' are utilities, which talk about interconnection queues as routine business. IREN is a miner turned AI data-centre operator. The comparables do not match.

Scaling ingest to about 20 more companies with TradingView catalogs and transcripts grows the dependence on the owner's display-only override and the 50-per-minute cap. Detection lives in transcripts, which the plan admits. That is exposure the owner holds, and the plan budgets it as free.

The proposed leakage test is weak. The judge and ticket 29 step 3 already refuse statements no Fact carries, so hindsight shows in which documents a session chooses to read, not in its statements. Two or three code false positives cannot separate good reading from memory of 2025.

It moves the 'main measure of the goal' from argued theses, which the owner bets on, to sentence detection. The plan's own risk list says code finds sentences, not theses, and cannot judge holder against buyer or financing (IREN's August against November). The measure then rewards the instrument for agreeing with its own vocabulary.

Blind Opus reviewers marking key cues for named companies (SanDisk, IREN) carry the same training-time knowledge of outcomes the plan uses against sessions. That matters less for sentence-level precision@20 but is not zero.

decision.dissent: Prospective-breadth's core point stands. Any 2025 replay is run by a model that read 2025, so isolation and closed-book probes measure the leak but cannot remove it, and seven cases with about two scored positives give a miss tally in which a single missing transcript can decide the verdict. Meanwhile the Q3 2026 earnings season is under way. Its transcripts are the only material neither the model's memory nor the case selection can touch, and every week of the Claude subscription spent on 2025 replays is a week not spent producing dated calls on bottlenecks the market has not yet priced. The record those calls would fill holds about one thesis cluster today. On that view the scorecard is an expensive diagnostic that may end with 'no class reached two', and the honest move is to widen live coverage now and let time do the scoring. The plan mitigates this but does not refute it. Isolation lets the memory-packaging Scout run in parallel; the SanDisk runs double as the second theme's first sessions; the photonics Researcher pause frees the budget; and the pre-registered fallback guarantees the runs end in a build decision.
